name: Retinol peel (Retinoic acid peel)

lead: A retinoic acid peel applies a tretinoin solution in a clinic, usually at around 5% strength in trials, to treat photoaging, melasma and similar concerns.
Research includes a placebo-controlled photoaging trial and laser comparisons in acanthosis nigricans, though a review describes the field as lacking consensus.

paras: Tretinoin is a retinoid used topically for acne, melasma, scars and aging; as a peel it is applied in higher concentrations to cause a controlled superficial exfoliation.
General peel risks include stinging, redness, dryness and pigment changes, rising with depth.

lead: A retinoic acid (tretinoin) peel is a superficial chemical peel in which a retinoid solution, often at 5% concentration in studies, is applied to the skin in a clinic and later washed off or left to act [1][2]. A review describes it as a superficial peeling frequently performed in dermatological clinics in Brazil, with a first study on melasma published in 2001 [1]. Wikipedia describes retinoic acid peels as deeper than alpha-hydroxy acid peels, used for scars, wrinkles and pigment, and often preceded by a Jessner's peel [3].

Evidence includes a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in facial photoaging and comparative trials in acanthosis nigricans [4][2][5]. A critical review states that studies have reported applicability with reasonable methodology but without a consistent scientific background or consensus [1].

paras: Reported uses include melasma, skin aging, acne, scars and photodamage, as topical tretinoin is used for various dermatoses [1]. Wikipedia lists scars, wrinkles and pigment [3].

In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 45 patients aged 35 to 70 with moderate-to-severe photodamage, participants received three microdermabrasion sessions followed by either a 5% retinoic acid peel or placebo, to evaluate efficacy and tolerability [2].

Two comparative studies, including a 2025 randomized controlled trial, examined fractional carbon dioxide laser versus a 5% retinoic acid peel for neck acanthosis nigricans [4][5]. A 2024 systematic review compared lasers with topical medications including peels for acanthosis nigricans [6]. A Brazilian review of tretinoin peels concluded the literature lacks consensus [1].

Wikipedia notes that complications rise with peel depth and can include prolonged redness, pigment changes, milia and skin thinning, and that light peels commonly cause stinging, redness, irritation and dryness. [3]

timeline.event: First published study of the tretinoin peel, for melasma, by Cuce et al. [1].
